change_summary: The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request, and its full text was replaced by a withdrawal statement. The stated reason is that the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. The stored paper's main results, such as the 2.1 °C lower peak indoor temperature and the 41% fewer hours above 28 °C, are based on those records, so the whole paper's findings cannot be relied on.
evaluation: Your Section 2.2 cites Okafor et al. [14] for the 2.1 °C green-roof indoor cooling value that you set in your model, and the stored paper reports that 2.1 °C figure. The withdrawal says the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on, which touches that parameter use. Your Discussion says the green-roof result scales almost directly with that 2.1 °C value, so it is touched too. The impact on your draft is high.
recommendation: Your Section 2.2 cites Okafor et al. [14] for the 2.1 °C green-roof indoor cooling value set in your model, and the current copy says the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. Your Discussion says the green-roof result scales almost directly with that 2.1 °C reduction. Stop and raise this with your co-authors or supervisor before going further, since the model depends on the value and editing the text won't fix it. Then replace or remove the citation and re-check the green-roof result it supports.
